afzalliklar.sub: Gain legal protection, partnership opportunities, and institutional development resources for your organization by joining the National Association of NGOs of Uzbekistan.
afzalliklar.about:
About the Association

National Association of Non-Governmental Non-Commercial Organizations of Uzbekistan (UzNANNGO)

UzNANNGO was state-registered by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan on 10 June 2005 under registration number 612.

The Association is a voluntary union of NGOs registered in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan, organized in the legal form of an NGO union.

Main goal: uniting local NGOs, coordinating, supporting, and developing their activities, and contributing to improving the effectiveness and quality of NGO work.

Registration date10 June 2005
Registration numberNo. 612
Legal address100170, Republic of Uzbekistan, Tashkent, Shaykhantakhur district, 1A Furqat Street
Organizational formUnion of non-governmental non-commercial organizations
afzalliklar.benefits:
What does the Association offer?

10 key areas your organization can take advantage of through membership.

Legal protection and representation

Representing and defending the rights and lawful interests of NGOs before state bodies, courts, and international and foreign organizations.

Developing cooperation

Participating in the development of mutually beneficial cooperation between NGOs, business entities, international and foreign organizations, and state bodies.

Creating an enabling environment

Helping to create favourable legal, economic, and social conditions for implementing NGO initiatives.

Supporting democratic processes

Uniting the efforts of members and partners to sustainably develop and promote democratic processes in the country.

Improving legislation

Participating in drafting legal and regulatory acts that affect NGO rights and lawful interests, and preparing proposals to improve sector legislation.

Building capacity

Raising NGO directors' and staff's knowledge and skills in effective organizational management, financial sustainability, designing socially important projects, volunteering, and attracting charitable resources.

Education and methodological support

Producing guides, curricula, and books for NGO representatives, plus theoretical and practical approaches suited to the country's conditions.

Social partnership

Maintaining a single database of state social orders and social-partnership projects; advancing economic, social, and cultural capacity in the country's modernization.

Supporting vulnerable populations

Mobilizing members' intellectual, material, and financial resources to support women, youth, the elderly, persons with disabilities, and citizens in difficult life situations.

International cooperation

Strengthening ties with international and foreign NGOs, financial institutions, and foreign donors, and learning from their positive experience.

foydalanishShartlari.title: Terms of use
foydalanishShartlari.sub: General rules for using the ngo.uz portal and its services.
foydalanishShartlari.body:
Last updated: 30 April 2026

By using the ngo.uz portal, you agree to the following terms. If any part of the terms does not work for you, please do not use the portal.

1. Key terms

  • Association — National Association of Non-Governmental Non-Commercial Organizations of Uzbekistan (UzNANNGO);
  • Portal — the official website at ngo.uz and its cabinet;
  • User — any natural or legal person using the portal;
  • Content — any text, image, video, document, or other information placed on the portal.

2. Use of the portal

Information and services on the portal are provided within the framework of the laws of the Republic of Uzbekistan, the Association's charter, and its code of ethics. The user:

  • Ensures the data they provide is accurate and complete;
  • Does not violate the rights of others;
  • Refrains from any action that harms the portal (server attacks, automated mass requests, viruses, etc.).

3. Account and password

Registration is required to use the portal cabinet. The user:

  • Keeps the password confidential and does not disclose it to third parties;
  • Is responsible for all actions taken through their account;
  • Promptly notifies the Association upon detecting any unauthorized access to their account.

4. Intellectual property

All portal content (logo, design, text, images, code) belongs to the Association unless otherwise indicated. Commercial use requires written permission. When quoting, the source (ngo.uz) must be cited.

5. Limitation of liability

The Association takes all reasonable measures to ensure the accuracy of the information posted, but:

  • Bears no responsibility for damage caused by technical malfunctions, downtime, or incomplete data;
  • Is not liable for the content of external sites linked from the portal;
  • Is not liable for situations arising from incorrect data entered by the user.

6. Privacy

Personal data is processed in accordance with the Privacy policy.

7. Changes to the terms

The Association reserves the right to unilaterally amend the terms of use. Updated terms take effect from the moment of publication on the portal.

8. Disputes

Any disputes related to use of the portal are resolved on the basis of the laws of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Before going to court, the parties must attempt to reach agreement through negotiation.

9. Contact

For questions about the terms of use, contact us:

  • Email: info@ngo.uz
  • Phone: (+998 55) 503-05-12

maxfiylikSiyosati.title: Privacy policy
maxfiylikSiyosati.sub: Personal data processing rules and user rights on the ngo.uz portal.
maxfiylikSiyosati.body:
Last updated: 30 April 2026

This document sets out the procedure for processing personal data collected via the ngo.uz portal by the National Association of Non-Governmental Non-Commercial Organizations of Uzbekistan (hereinafter — "the Association", "we"). It has been developed in accordance with the Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan "On Personal Data".

1. Data we collect

The following data may be collected while using the portal and its services:

  • Data you provide — first and last name, phone number, email, organization name, and certificate number;
  • Additional information from inquiry and reporting forms;
  • Technical data — IP address, browser type, login time, and page-navigation statistics on the portal.

2. Purposes of data use

Collected data is used only for the following purposes:

  • Association membership and service delivery;
  • Responding to inquiries, questions, and complaints;
  • Statistical analysis and improving portal quality;
  • Other cases provided for by law.

3. Transfer to third parties

Personal data is not transferred to third parties without the user's consent. Exceptions:

  • At the request of the law and the official request of authorized state bodies;
  • Technical service providers (over an encrypted channel, under strict confidentiality terms).

4. Data retention period

Data is retained until the purpose of processing is fulfilled. You may request removal of your data (see clause 4).

5. User rights

You have the following rights:

  • Access and correction of data about yourself;
  • Withdraw consent;
  • Request deletion of data;
  • Object to processing.

6. Cookies

The portal uses cookies to improve user experience, maintain session state, and for statistical analysis. You can disable them in browser settings, but this may affect some portal functionality.

7. Security measures

Data is transmitted via HTTPS encryption and stored on secured servers. Our staff have access to personal data only within the scope of their duties.

8. Changes

This policy may be updated from time to time. The updated version is published on this page, with the effective date shown above.

9. Contact

For any questions about your data, contact us:

  • Email: info@ngo.uz
  • Phone: (+998 55) 503-05-12
  • Address: 100170, Tashkent, Shaykhantakhur district, 1A Furqat Street
  • Or via the inquiry form.

sustainabilityCert.title: "Sustainable NGO"
sustainabilityCert.sub: Open list of NGOs that received the sustainability index certificate
sustainabilityCert.body:
The "Sustainable NGO" certificate is an official recognition awarded to organizations that score high on the sustainability index. It is issued in three tiers: Tier 3, Tier 2, and Tier 1. It confirms the organization's reliability and gives an advantage in grants and partnership with the state.

Tier and statistics figures will appear here once the official registry of certified organizations is connected.

Certificate tiers

Tier 3

Tier 3 certificate

For organizations that meet the basic sustainability requirements. Governance and financial-transparency systems are in place.

60–79 points on the sustainability index
Tier 2

Tier 2 certificate

Organizations that have proven their sustainability through strong governance, financial stability, and effective programmes.

80–89 points on the sustainability index
Tier 1

Tier 1 certificate

The highest recognition for NGOs that score highly across all criteria and lead their sector.

90–100 points on the sustainability index

Certified organizations

Registry — 2024

A tier-based filter will be added once the registry is connected.

How to apply for certification

4 steps

Follow these steps to obtain the certificate.

  1. Submit an application

    Fill out the assessment application via the member cabinet and upload the required documents.

  2. Document review

    UzNANNGO specialists review all materials and may request additional information.

  3. On-site assessment

    If required, the organization's activities are observed on site and scored.

  4. Certificate issuance

    At a score of 60 points or above, the corresponding tier certificate is formally awarded.

sustainabilityIndex.title: NGO sustainability index (planned project)
sustainabilityIndex.sub: System for assessing the institutional sustainability of NGOs in Uzbekistan
sustainabilityIndex.body:
The NGO sustainability index is a tool that assesses an organization's long-term viability across six core criteria. The index is calculated annually by UzNANNGO and the results are published openly. The aim: help NGOs identify their strengths and weaknesses and set development directions.

The number of assessed NGOs and average score figures will appear here once the index registry is connected.

Assessment criteria

Six criteria, 100 points total

Maximum points are shown per criterion.

Governance and transparency

Council structure, annual reports, financial audit, and internal-control systems.

max 20 points

Financial sustainability

Diversity of funding, financial reserves, and effective budget management.

max 20 points

Programme effectiveness

Activity outcomes, beneficiary count, and the social impact of projects.

max 20 points

Human resources

Staff retention, professional development, volunteers, and personnel capacity.

max 15 points

Cooperation and network

Ties with state bodies, the business community, and international organizations.

max 15 points

Infrastructure and IT

Website, social networks, databases, and management systems.

max 10 points

Levels

Developing — 0–39 points
Growing — 40–59 points
Consolidating — 60–79 points
Sustainable — 80–100 points

mission.title: Mission and objectives
mission.sub: UzNANNGO's mission, priority directions and strategic goals.
mission.body:
Mission

The National Association of Non-Governmental Non-Commercial Organizations of Uzbekistan (UzNANNGO) was established in 2005 to strengthen civil society, develop the non-governmental sector, and raise the legal, organizational and professional capacity of NGOs. The Association operates in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan and has become the coordination centre of the NGO sector.

Main goals

  1. Support the activities of non-governmental non-commercial organizations and strengthen their role in society.
  2. Ensure dialogue and cooperation between civil society institutions and state bodies.
  3. Develop transparency, sustainability and professional governance in the NGO sector.
  4. Strengthen the global integration of Uzbekistan's civil society through international cooperation.

Main objectives

  1. Strengthen NGOs' legal status, defend their interests before state bodies, and submit proposals to improve legislation.
  2. Raise the professional skills of NGO directors and staff; organize training courses, seminars and workshops.
  3. Analyse the activities of civil society institutions, conduct monitoring and develop practical recommendations.
  4. Ensure information exchange among NGOs and bring their activities to the wider public.
  5. Establish relations with international organizations and foreign partners; implement cooperation programmes.
  6. Calculate the NGO sustainability index and run the "Sustainable NGO" certification system.
  7. Develop government–civil-society partnership; design proposals and projects to improve social-order mechanisms.

Functions

  1. Coordination: coordinate the activities of regional branches, member organizations and partner institutions.
  2. Database: maintain the registry of NGOs in Uzbekistan and collect and analyse data on their activities.
  3. Education: systematic training and skill-raising through the "NGO School" programme.
  4. Legal aid: consult member organizations on registration, reporting and compliance with legislation.
  5. Cooperation: implement joint projects with UNDP, USAID, GIZ, UNICEF and other international organizations.
  6. Monitoring: track the development dynamics of the NGO sector and prepare reports.

Strategic goals (2026–2028)

  1. Strengthen the regional network — ensure active branches operate in all 14 regions and Karakalpakstan.
  2. Digitalize services — introduce online membership, electronic reporting and interactive services.
  3. Raise analytical capacity — expand the quality and coverage of the annual NGO sustainability index.

whoWeAre.title: National Association of NGOs of Uzbekistan
whoWeAre.body:
The National Association of Non-Governmental Non-Commercial Organizations of Uzbekistan (UzNANNGO) is a national body established to strengthen civil society, coordinate NGO activities and support them. Registered with the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan, it has operated since 2019.

The Association's main objectives include developing recommendations to improve the legal environment for NGOs, strengthening the cooperation between the non-governmental sector and state bodies, supporting the growth of NGOs' organizational capacity, and expanding their international cooperation.

The Association works closely with the Oliy Majlis of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the executive authorities. It actively participates in discussions of legislative initiatives related to civil society and regularly submits analytical materials and proposals on the NGO sector to the relevant authorities.

“Our main goal is to defend the legal rights of every non-governmental non-commercial organization in Uzbekistan, strengthen their role in society, and contribute meaningfully to the formation of a sustainable civil society.”
— Head of the UzNANNGO Executive Office

The Association's NGO registry serves as a venue for sharing knowledge, gaining experience and establishing cooperation. Through the NGO School, the online library and regional trainings, methodological and practical support reaches hundreds of organizations. At the same time, research, talks and open discussions are held with representatives of the business community, academia and international organizations.

The Association was founded to unite all NGOs in Uzbekistan, defend their interests and contribute to the formation of a healthy civil society in our country. The Executive Office is located in Tashkent — on Furqat Street in the Shaykhantakhur district; 28 regional staff operate across all regions of the republic.

about.goal:
Main goal

The Association's main goal is to unite local NGOs, coordinate, support, and develop their activities, and contribute to improving the effectiveness and quality of NGO work.
about.tasks:
Main objectives

The Association acts in the interests of its members and civil society in the following areas.

1

Legal protection and representation

Representing and defending the rights and lawful interests of NGOs before state bodies, courts, and international and foreign organizations.

2

Developing cooperation

Participating in the development of mutually beneficial cooperation between NGOs, business entities, international and foreign organizations, and state bodies.

3

Creating an enabling environment

Helping create favourable legal, economic, and social conditions for implementing NGO initiatives.

4

Supporting democratic processes

Uniting the efforts of members and partners to sustainably develop and promote democratic processes in the country.

5

Improving legislation

Participating in drafting legal and regulatory acts that affect NGO rights and lawful interests, and preparing proposals to improve sector legislation.

6

Building capacity

Raising NGO directors' and staff's knowledge and skills in effective organizational management, financial sustainability, designing socially important projects, volunteering, and attracting charitable resources.

7

Education and methodological support

Producing guides, curricula, and books for NGO representatives, plus theoretical and practical approaches suited to the country's conditions.

8

Social partnership

Maintaining a single database of state social orders and social-partnership projects; advancing economic, social, and cultural capacity in the country's modernization.

9

Supporting vulnerable populations

Mobilizing members' intellectual, material, and financial resources to support women, youth, the elderly, persons with disabilities, and citizens in difficult life situations.

10

International cooperation

Strengthening ties with international and foreign NGOs, financial institutions, and foreign donors, and learning from their positive experience.

membershipGuide.title: How to join
membershipGuide.sub: Complete the membership process step by step.
membershipGuide.stepsHtml:
Step 1: Prepare documents

Prepare the organization's certificate, TIN, director's details and contact information.

Step 2: Review the regulations

Review the membership terms and the rights-and-obligations set.

Step 3: Submit the online form

Fill in and submit the application in the "Join" section.

Step 4: Review and decision

The application is reviewed within the timelines set by the charter; the status appears on the page.

Step 5: Certificate

After a positive decision, the membership certificate is issued.

membershipModal.title: Join the Association
membershipModal.subtitle: Fill out the application to join the National Association of NGOs of Uzbekistan
membershipModal.terms1: Admission to the National Association of Non-Governmental Non-Commercial Organizations of Uzbekistan (UzNANNGO) is carried out on the basis of the UzNANNGO Charter.
membershipModal.terms2: The purpose of membership is the development of civil society, ensuring the legal protection of NGOs, raising staff capacity and expanding international cooperation.
membershipModal.terms3: Member organizations have the following rights: participation in Association events, access to trainings and seminars, discussion of Council decisions, and voting.
membershipModal.terms4: Member organizations fulfil the following obligations: payment of the annual membership fee, submission of an annual activity report, and compliance with Association decisions.
membershipModal.terms5: After the application is reviewed, UzNANNGO sends a letter on membership. The decision is made within 15 business days.
